samples.summary: Escaping test asserts against `mysql.escape` output, mirroring the implementation instead of the escaped SQL
samples.evidence: The test computes `const escaped = mysql.escape(hostile)` (line 77) and then asserts `q.totalViews` contains `document_id = ${escaped}` — while `sql()` in analytics-warehouse.service.ts is literally `return mysql.escape(value)`. Expected and actual are produced by the same function, so the assertion can only detect that the builder still calls mysql2's escaper; it cannot detect that the result is actually safe (a hypothetical identity escaper would keep the test green). Same pattern at line 102 in the workspace roll-up test, where a previously literal expectation (`'d''2'`) was replaced by `mysql.escape("d'2")`. A literal expected string (e.g. containing `\'` and `\\`) would pin the observable escaping behaviour rather than the call.

samples.summary: New `canManage: false` default in `documentRows` has no test
samples.evidence: `documentRows` now emits `canManage: false` on every warehouse row, but analytics-warehouse.service.spec.ts (read in full, 135 lines) only exercises `buildQueries`/`buildWorkspaceQueries` and the disabled/empty-workspace paths — no test drives `documentRows` (it needs `this.pool!.query`). Impact is limited because the controller overwrites the field, but the warehouse's own default is unasserted.

samples.summary: No test for a warehouse row with no matching Postgres document (title fallback + `canManage` from `authorID ?? null`)
samples.evidence: The controller falls back to `title: d?.title ?? r.documentId` and `isDocumentManager(member.role, d?.authorID ?? null, userId)` when `meta.get(r.documentId)` misses. In analytics.controller.spec.ts the prisma mock always returns docs matching both warehouse rows (`d1`, `d2`), so neither fallback branch is exercised — notably an owner would get `canManage: true` for an unknown document id, which nothing asserts either way.
